BABY BEATERS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
just how safe are your children in the care of nanny? We speak exclusively to the parents in the assault case caught on camera.

Summary:
A Welkom domestic worker has been arrested after she was caught on video allegedly beating her employers' 7-month-old baby boy.

We speak to the parents exclusively and have access to the full 60 minute video.



Further information:
THE STORY
Lieutenant-Colonel Thando Mbambo said the worker Mafsehediso Lisbeth Makashea appeared in the Welkom Magistrate's Court, in the Free State, on 23 December and was released on R1 000 bail. She would appear again on 29 January.

The child's mother told the newspaper she went shopping with her 6-year-old child on 21 December, and she set up a camera in her living room where Makashea was left to look after the baby.

She reportedly said she previously had a bad experience with a former domestic worker and wanted to see for her own peace of mind how Makashea treated her children when she was not at home.

INTERVIEWS
ANNA-MI & ORG LINDE - parents in Welkom case
ANN SKELTON - Centre for Child Law - the legal angle
PSYCHOLOGIST - the mind of an abuser
DR LORNA JACKLIN - the medical implications
NANNY CAMS ALL THE RAGE - we look at an increase in sales of these types of cameras - and ask why families are choosing to keep an eye on nannies.
POLICE - the Welkom family not happy with how the case is being handled - not being taken seriously




Extra Budget Items:
Travel to Welkom

Locations:
Welkom & Johannesburg

Press Release:


Baby beaters
A shocking video of a Ugandan nanny viciously abusing a toddler went viral at the end of last year, causing outrage from a global online public who openly bayed for her blood. But, the video encouraged a Welkom couple to also monitor the nanny hired to care for their 7-month-old baby. What their cameras recorded shocked them to the core. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


BABY BEATERS STRUCTURE

VO: Many South African parents leave their children in the care of nannies every single day. But very few know what really happens when they’re not there.

UPSOUND WELKOM VIDEO: BABY CRYING – NANNY PUSHING IT DOWN

ANNE-MI: that cry of him, he was looking for help, he was looking for us, where, where were we? We weren’t here

VO: Parents Anna-Mi & Org Linde recorded this video on the 21st of December at their home in Welkom, in the Free State. Their 7 month old son Nico was in the care of a nanny, seen here doing exactly what all parents dread.

Even child experts were horrified.

LORNA: This baby would be somebody that has been in a boxing ring, that has been hit and concussed.
GAIDA: it goes against everything that we are naturally inclined to do in a situation like that.

VO: The Linde’s put up a camera because their baby had been behaving strangely.

ANNE-MI: He had a thing that he was shaking his head, and he struggled to sleep// He would wake up quite frequently
ORG: He started slapping you, pinching you, started going for your face, scratching you.

VO: Anna-Mi, a nurse and her husband, Org, an assistant supermarket manager both work shifts. Their children, Sarika aged 6 and baby Nico spend some of the time home alone with a nanny.

They had suspicions about a recently employed nanny, so while Org was at work, Anna-Mi recorded the goings on at their house while she went out with Sarika.

The hour long video confirmed their worst fears.

ANNA-MI: you never thought that you are going to see anything – I wasn’t even 12 minutes into the video when I saw her first pulling him on the arm and pushing him back on the pillow. It felt like someone was choking me, you can’t breathe, I wanted to, I wanted to die

VO: Anna-Mi was hysterical, Org came home immediately to watch the rest of the video - he was mortified by what he saw.

ORG: It still breaks my heart, I can’t sleep at night, I can’t. Every time when I see him he starts laughing and smiling, all that images goes through my head the whole time.

VO: We showed the video clip to Developmental Paediatrician Professor Lorna Jacklin.

LORNA: A baby’s cry is a form of communication. This baby is crying out of fear, it is no longer communicating, that is the cry of a baby that is absolutely terrified.

VO: At this young age, being hit on the head like this can damage a child both emotionally and physically.

LORNA: This baby is at a very high risk of having brain damage // a baby is not built to be thrown around in that way, //she throws it around and it settles down, it keeps quiet, because it’s been concussed by this throwing it around

VO: Shaken baby syndrome, or non-accidental head injury, is often fatal and can cause brain damage.

LORNA: The brain of a baby floats in fluid and as you throw the baby, you’ve got the skull and brain moving at different rates, so // you get bleeding of the little vessels that connect the brain to the skull.

VO: Although baby Nico had been given the all clear after scans and physical examinations, Anna-Mi still blames herself for not doing proper background checks.

ANNA-MI: I trusted this lady with my flesh and blood, I let her into my house, it’s not him that let her into my house, I let her, I trusted her

VO: Professor Ann Skelton from the Centre for Child Law believes child care abuse is rife. It’s just not reported.

ANN: There are high levels of violence in communities through out SA and the more stressed families are the more likely there is to be outbursts of violence amongst caregivers,

VO: And it’s not only happening here. Suspicious parents around the world are installing cameras.

In India last year a hidden camera caught a nanny repeatedly shaking and tossing a child about.

This Ugandan video went viral in November – exposing a nanny’s violent assault on a two year old - after she’d thrown up on the floor.

The brutality in this clip is so extreme we cannot show this in its entirety during family viewing time. The nanny continued to beat, kick and even stepped on the traumatized child. The nanny was sentenced to 4 years in jail for child abuse.

Clinical Psychologist Dr. Giada Del Fabbro says the Welkom nanny isn’t showing normal adult frustration with a fractious baby.

GAIDA: we need to look at the intensity and level of aggression we see in that video – it’s not just a nanny getting frustrated or rolling her eyes, or sighing, or maybe even shouting at the child – which would be all the degrees of frustration that could be quite normal if a child is crying and they won’t settle down – but you see this goes from zero to a hundred.

VO: She says not all women are suited to childcare, but are forced to take on whatever job they can get.

GAIDA: It’s a faulty assumption, a woman comes with a certain set of factors in her background that may really impair that ability and this may be a really desperate means of gaining some sort of financial remuneration and it’s not really a calling // it’s a job like any other and there may be a lot of resentment for having to do something they don't want to do.

VO: Although the nanny has been arrested and charged with assault, the Linde’s aren’t convinced the police understand the severity of such cases.

ORG: The way the police treated us, I am now second guessing myself. // am I just a parent that saw this and now blowing the thing out of proportion – I don't know anymore. // Because the way that they are handling it – it’s blasé.

VO: Welkom Police Spokesperson Lebo Lechasa says the police are serious about child abuse cases and will prioritize baby Nico’s case.

MOLEBOGENG: I will immediately contact the investigating officer and the commander to ensure that they meet the family. Yah, we will definitely work hard on this case, yah.

VO: The nanny, Tshidi Makashea, has appeared in court and was released on bail of a thousand rands, which some members of the public feel is too lenient.

VOX POP 1 (black lady) I am absolutely livid that someone could treat someone else’s child like that
VOX POP 2 (white woman) It’s completely shocking cant believe she was bail.
VOX POP 3 (white man) It’s disgusting that someone could be given bail for a thousand rand after seeing that video. Where is the justice system going?

ANN: I can understand the public anger, because obviously people are feeling this is a unacceptable crime, which it certainly is. Bail is part of our criminal law process, people even get bail for murder in some cases. // They look at what is affordable for the person, because essentially if you ask a domestic worker to pay R50 000 bail, that person is just simply never going to be able to pay bail.

VO: We called the nanny in an attempt to find out what led her to act in this manner.

DEVI: Why did you do that to that baby?
TSIDI: The baby just want to fall, I just want to help the baby, the parents of the baby don’t want to accept that
DEVI: You were helping the baby? That’s not helping?
TSIDI: The baby want to fall, I just want to pick up the baby.

VO: The nanny has opened a counter charge of assault, claiming that Anna-Mi burnt her with an iron on her stomach. Anna-Mi denies the allegation.

ANN: Well, if someone assaults you, you are entitled to fight back, but you’re not entitled to go hit that person’s child in retaliation – that would be never be defensible in the law.

VO: Professor Skelton believes the video evidence will strengthen the case if properly presented in court.

A guilty verdict could mean jail time and also see her being declared unsuitable to work with children. The Department of Social Development keeps such a register.

Horror nanny abuse videos have boosted Nanny-cams sales worldwide.

LINK: It’s really simple all you need is a camera, an internet connection and you could be big brother in your own home.

VO: Young mom, Claudine Readings saw a gap in the market and began importing them three years ago. Business is booming.

In houses with baby cams, nannies can’t even sleep on the job.

CLAUDINE: the day after we’ve sold them, we’ve had calls, not necessarily for abuse case, but the nanny’s been sleeping on the case, left the baby in the cot – but they’re not doing their jobs.

VO: Claudine caught her hired help cat napping when she was meant to be keeping an eye on her twin daughters.

CLAUDINE: you don’t know what is going on behind closed doors. And as much as you want to trust someone you can’t. You think that things are going to be fine – you just don’t know.

VO: Prof. Jacklin. says for those who can’t afford the technology, vigilance is the key.

LORNA: Any change in your child’s behaviour. // Be suspicious, if you leave home and you;re baby’s fine and you come home and your baby is irritable – what happened during the day and if it continues then you just have say well, there is something wrong.
ORG: Trust your instincts, if you feel something is wrong, trust it, follow up






PROMO 1
VO: Just how safe are your children in the care of nanny when you’re not there?

ANNE-MI: that cry of him, he was looking for help, he was looking for us, where, where were we?

VO: We speak exclusively to the parents in the South African baby assault caught on camera.

PROMO 2 (10 seconds)
VO: This horrific video exposes a Welkom Nanny abusing a 7-month old child.

LORNA: This baby would be somebody that has been in a boxing ring, that has been hit and concussed.


PROMO 3

VO: Leaving your children in the hands of caregiver could be more of risk than you could ever imagine.

CLAUDINE: you don’t know what is going on behind closed doors. And as much as you want to trust someone you can’t.

VO: Carte Blanche investigates Nanny abuse.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): just how safe are your children in the care of nanny? We speak exclusively to the parents in the assault case caught on camera.
metadata.Summary: A Welkom domestic worker has been arrested after she was caught on video allegedly beating her employers' 7-month-old baby boy. We speak to the parents exclusively and have access to the full 60 minute video.
metadata.Further information: THE STORY Lieutenant-Colonel Thando Mbambo said the worker Mafsehediso Lisbeth Makashea appeared in the Welkom Magistrate's Court, in the Free State, on 23 December and was released on R1 000 bail. She would appear again on 29 January. The child's mother told the newspaper she went shopping with her 6-year-old child on 21 December, and she set up a camera in her living room where Makashea was left to look after the baby. She reportedly said she previously had a bad experience with a former domestic worker and wanted to see for her own peace of mind how Makashea treated her children when she was not at home. INTERVIEWS ANNA-MI & ORG LINDE - parents in Welkom case ANN SKELTON - Centre for Child Law - the legal angle PSYCHOLOGIST - the mind of an abuser DR LORNA JACKLIN - the medical implications NANNY CAMS ALL THE RAGE - we look at an increase in sales of these types of cameras - and ask why families are choosing to keep an eye on nannies. POLICE - the Welkom family not happy with how the case is being handled - not being taken seriously
